primitives.name: Tournament Score Feasibility
primitives.verbatim_quote: ≤ s_m is a tournament score sequence iff Σ_{i=1}^k s_i ≥ binomial(k,2) for 1 ≤ k ≤ m and Σ_{i=1}^m s_i = binomial(m,2).
primitives.latex: \sum_{i=1}^{k} s_i \geq \binom{k}{2} \text{ for } 1 \leq k \leq m \text{ and } \sum_{i=1}^{m} s_i = \binom{m}{2}
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s_i': 'out-degree of vertex i (dimensionless)', 'k': 'index of partial sum (dimensionless)', 'm': 'number of vertices (dimensionless)', 'binomial(k,2)': 'combinatorial count of edges in k-node clique (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Complete round-robin tournament with no draws; every pair of teams plays exactly once.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When score set violates Landau's inequalities or total edge count mismatch.

layer2.mapping: Score sequence is isomorphic to a tournament graph's out-degree vector under Landau's constraint.
layer2.telemetry: Verification of inequality constraints and total edge consistency.

primitives.name: Reid Conjecture Verification
primitives.verbatim_quote: Reid's 1978 conjecture (every set of nonnegative integers is the score set of some tournament; proved non-constructively by Yao 1989) is verified constructively for the tested cases.
primitives.assumptions: Every finite set of non-negative integers can represent a tournament score set.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When a set fails to admit a valid tournament construction.

layer2.mapping: Constructive proof of Reid\'s conjecture provides kernel for generating valid score sequences.
layer2.telemetry: Algorithmic generation of tournament from arbitrary integer sets.

primitives.name: Polynomial Reconstruction Algorithm
primitives.verbatim_quote: Research question Given only the *score set* of a tournament (the set of distinct out-degrees, not the full score sequence), when can a valid score sequence be reconstructed, and can it be done in polynomial time?
primitives.assumptions: Input is a finite set of distinct integers representing tournament out-degrees.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When input set is not a valid tournament score set or algorithm exceeds polynomial complexity.

layer2.mapping: Algorithmic reconstruction maps score set to full sequence using derived combinatorial bounds.
layer2.telemetry: Runtime performance and correctness of reconstructed sequences.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core challenge lies in reconstructing a tournament score sequence from its score set under Landau's theorem. This involves verifying that the sum of first k elements meets binomial(k,2) lower bound and that total sum equals binomial(m,2). The Reid conjecture ensures such a sequence exists for any valid integer set, but the paper provides constructive proof. The algorithmic solution must ensure polynomial-time reconstruction while maintaining combinatorial validity. Failure modes include violation of Landau's inequalities or incorrect handling of degenerate cases where multiple sequences map to same score set. The model assumes complete, no-draw tournaments, which excludes real-world complexities like NFL scheduling.
